methods.label: Combine the reciprocal terms
methods.explanation:
Combine the two reciprocal terms first. Their denominators form a sum-and-difference pair, so their product simplifies by the difference-of-squares identity:
\[
(2+\sqrt2)(\sqrt2-2)
=(\sqrt2)^2-2^2=-2.
\]
In particular, neither denominator is zero. Using their product as a common denominator gives
\[
\frac1{2+\sqrt2}+\frac1{\sqrt2-2}
=\frac{(\sqrt2-2)+(2+\sqrt2)}{-2}
=-\sqrt2.
\]
Hence the entire expression is
\[
2+\sqrt2-\sqrt2=2,
\]
which is choice A.
